label: STOPP F7
title: Antipsychotic with swallowing difficulty
statement: Antipsychotics with dysphagia (increased risk of aspiration pneumonia).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: An antipsychotic medicine in a person who has trouble swallowing (dysphagia) raises the risk of food or fluid going into the lungs and causing pneumonia.

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotic medicines
medicine_groups.note: Tablets, orally dissolving tablets, capsules, liquids and the listed long-acting injections count. Clopixol Acuphase also counts when supplied for short-term treatment. Generic packs showing a listed ingredient with a company name count for the same forms. Prochlorperazine and metoclopramide are not in this group. Saphris sublingual wafers count.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only when the patient was aged 65 years or older at the supply being assessed. If age is unknown, ask for age confirmation before attributing a STOPP finding. With a Group A antipsychotic supply, suspect a finding if a diagnosis, result or swallowing assessment documents dysphagia during exposure. Accept a pharmacist answer confirming difficulty swallowing during this treatment. Cite the relevant line and the supply. If swallowing during this treatment is unknown, report a possible finding and name the missing fact exactly as "Dysphagia (difficulty swallowing)". Clear the finding for an exposure when swallowing was documented as normal then.

needs_facts.meets: A diagnosis, result, swallowing assessment or pharmacist answer documents difficulty swallowing during this antipsychotic treatment.

options.words: Had difficulty swallowing during this antipsychotic treatment
Swallowed normally during this antipsychotic treatment

cannot_be_seen: Whether the person has trouble swallowing if the record holds no line about it, why the antipsychotic was started, and the dose actually taken. Also medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the person has any difficulty swallowing, and whether the antipsychotic is still needed.
